resolutions: Direct, causative, and applicative objects have alike surface carriers but distinct typed functions.
A direct object is governed by its directive lexical Source.
A causative or applicative object is governed by the matching derivational operation and its suffix.
The causative or applicative object plus suffix is a discontinuous grammatical unit derived from history.
The user chooses the actual Source, valence, participant, and operation rather than an object-function switch.
Any open Source may receive a user-intended exceptional intransitive analysis; Canvas examples never authorize a stem list.
A causative-shaped spelling does not by itself force a causative analysis or block an intransitive analysis.
Each participant-adding causative or applicative operation contributes exactly one complete Valence position.
A directive Source retains its original direct object when later participant-adding operations apply.
The application derives one-, two-, or three-object structure from the actual composition without an object-count control.
Every Valence position is structurally complete rather than a printed placeholder.
A fourth object position is blocked.
An intransitive Source starts with no object and gains objects only through its selected participant-adding operations.
Derivational levels must be unique and contiguous.
The newest object in the history is automatically mainline.
Every earlier object remains automatically shuntline at its proper level.
Derivational history and mainline status are distinct from later surface object order.
No level, prominence, history-schema, slot-count, or Canvas-example control is added.
A directive Source object remains the first position in its derivational history.
Each later causative or applicative operation adds its own participant at the next level.
The retained direct object becomes shuntline when a newer object is added.
An extremely limited third-stage causative history is blocked unless the intended Source meaning supports it.
Meaning support authorizes the intended history and never creates a stem whitelist.
Every Valence position and subposition remains structurally filled even when it has no sounded carrier.
Exactly one object position is mainline.
A reflexive object has the mainline reflexive shape only when it is the privileged newest object.
An earlier reflexive object remains a shuntline ne position.
The last-added suffix normally determines the mainline reflexive position automatically.
Causative-before-applicative is the ordinary suffix history.
Applicative-before-later-causative requires genuine exceptional-order support.
Suffix history and surface object-pronoun order remain separate projections.
When specific projectives are incompatible, only the privileged one sounds.
A silenced specific projective remains a complete typed position rather than disappearing.
No carrier, silence, subposition, suffix-order, or reflexive-prominence switch is exposed.
The shared multiple-object formula is projected from complete typed Valence positions.
Every dyadic position retains both subpositions even when both are silent.
The newest mainline specific object is privileged over an incompatible specific shuntline object.
A first- or second-person specific shuntline carrier and a third-singular one become 0-0 when silenced.
A silenced third-plural shuntline carrier keeps 0-im unless the privileged specific object is also third plural.
When both specific objects are third plural, the shuntline carrier is 0-0.
A specific shuntline object remains sounded when the mainline object is nonspecific or reflexive, except for a separately authorized later variant.
Nonspecific human tē and nonhuman tla carriers remain automatic ordinary Valence realizations.
A shuntline reflexive or reciprocal has the automatic ne realization.
The user supplies participants but never chooses formula positions or silent carriers.
Object carriers are universally ordered by form rather than direct, causative, or applicative function.
Specific carriers precede reflexive and nonspecific carriers; reflexive precedes nonspecific; human tē precedes nonhuman tla.
All thirteen three-carrier combinations are canonical results of the same ordering rule rather than chart-row options.
Every valid two-carrier sequence preserves the order of its corresponding three-carrier row.
Direction retains its existing Lesson 8 position inside the complete multiple-object formula.
Two reflexive positions can realize as mainline m-o plus shuntline ne.
Silent participants remain recoverable from typed Source valence and derivational history.
A role-mapping choice is exposed only when distinct valid mappings yield the identical visible carrier sequence; otherwise typed composition fixes it automatically.
